note: Full worldwide sweep of ancient-site classes from Wikidata (query.wikidata.org/sparql). Each class is items with wdt:P31/wdt:P279* the QID (instance or subclass, transitively) that carry a P625 coordinate. Wikidata's own data is CC0 (see https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing); per-image Commons licences are resolved separately, as for the curated sample (wikidata-enrich.mjs). Classes are listed in dedupe precedence order: an item matching more than one class keeps the earlier class's type. Confirmed by an ASK query: stone circle (Q1935728) is a transitive subclass of megalith (Q164240), so the specific classes that map to a DIFFERENT type than the generic megalith catch-all (stone-circle -> circle) must come before it, or every stone circle would be swallowed into type megalith. dolmen is not a P279* subclass of megalith at all; menhir is, but menhir also maps to megalith, so its position relative to the catch-all does not matter. type maps onto the existing glyph taxonomy in public/ancient-sites (megalith renders as the trilith glyph; circle, mound, settlement and geoglyph glyphs match their type name). QIDs were verified by label against the Wikidata search API on 26 September 2026 -- see task-1-report.md for the ones the initial brief had wrong.
